subject: 3B0211B4DCD4EA86BB1FC4BB6ADCD7C3
introduction: These hundred prayers ask God for protection: from oppressors, from tests too strong to bear, and, just as often, from oneself, “from turning to any one but Thee”. Many were written for communities under attack, and a number go on to pray for the attackers. The Psalms are the great store of such prayer, with their shield, wings, tower and shadow; the Qur’an’s last two chapters are prayers of refuge said daily by Muslims; and the Lord’s Prayer ends “deliver us from evil”. The imprecatory psalms, which ask God to break the enemy, are the tradition these prayers decline to follow.
questions: From what do these prayers ask protection? Which dangers are outside the person and which within?
Several prayers ask good for the oppressor. Is that harder or easier than asking for safety?
Does praying for protection make a person more careful, or less?

outside.why: Make Thy protection my armoury, Thy preservation my shield. The Lord God is a sun and shield.
Is there any Remover of difficulties save God? God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
’Neath the shade of Thy protecting wings let me nestle. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust.
Begin to pray and repent, and implore protection. Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.
In the hands of oppressors. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me.
I call on Thee, imploring protection. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak, from the evil of that which He created.
Cleaving fast to Thy Name. The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
Keep them safe from turning to any but Thee: the danger asked against is inward. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
They have fallen victim to oppression. Pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.
Make known to those who hate. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.

The Psalter’s prayers for protection often asked more: break their teeth, O God, in their mouth. These prayers ask that enemies be enlightened. What does it cost to pray so for people who are doing one harm?

shortfall: Ninety of the hundred prayers ask refuge in God in closely similar terms; companions were set to the distinct images of the first stretches only.
